headline: African LNG Exports Projected to Rise 175% by 2030
summary: The African Energy Chamber forecasts a 175% increase in LNG exports as energy buyers seek alternatives to the Strait of Hormuz. Upstream investment is expected to reach $40 billion annually through 2030, boosting total hydrocarbon output to 12.5 million boe/d.
why: Africa is increasingly viewed as a critical alternative energy supplier for global markets looking to diversify away from Middle Eastern transit routes, which are subject to geopolitical volatility.
why_moved: The projected surge in supply from Africa provides a significant alternative to traditional Middle Eastern energy sources, likely impacting global LNG pricing benchmarks.
